title: Jon Abrahams to Direct True Survival Drama Merry Christmas, Jay
excerpt:
The film draws on a mechanic's rescue of 24 people during a Christmas blizzard.
Ryan March wrote the screenplay and will produce.
body_md:
Jon Abrahams, known for his roles in Scary Movie and Meet the Parents, is attached to direct a drama inspired by mechanic Jay Withey's actions during the deadly Christmas blizzard of 2022.

According to the project's description, Withey was stranded in his vehicle with two strangers on Christmas Eve. He broke a window at a school in Cheektowaga, New York, to find shelter, then repeatedly returned outside to help other stranded motorists. The account describes 75 trips into the storm and 24 people finding shelter in the school.

The title comes from the apology note Withey left for the damaged windows, which he signed with a Christmas greeting and his name. It connects the film directly to the real event.

Abrahams previously directed two features in Buffalo and emphasizes the humanity of the city and Withey's story. Ryan March acquired the rights to tell the story, wrote the screenplay and will produce through Altruistic Films.

The project remains in development, with Sig De Miguel and Steven Vincent attached as casting directors. No cast, production schedule or release date has been announced.
